# myestateaccess

> Visitor management for gated residential estates in Nigeria. A resident generates a short one-time code, sends it to their visitor by WhatsApp or SMS, and the guard verifies it at the gate — including when there is no internet connection.

At most estate gates today, a visitor names a house and the guard phones the
resident (or the visitor phones their host from the gate) before letting them
in. myestateaccess replaces that call. The problems it exists to solve are that
an unanswered call leaves a visitor stuck at the gate, that a house number
proves nothing about who the resident expected, and that nobody can say
afterwards who was let in, by whom, or on whose word.

The same platform collects estate dues: residents pay in the app and landlords
from an emailed link, and the money settles into the estate's own bank account.

Visitors install nothing and create no account. They receive a code in a
message and read it out at the gate.

## Key facts

- Visitor codes are **single use**. Once accepted at the gate a code is spent; a second attempt is refused and recorded as a double-entry attempt for the estate manager to review.
- Codes **expire after six hours**, whether or not anyone arrives. Expiry is automatic and needs no action from the resident.
- A resident may hold **up to three live codes** at once.
- **Verification works offline.** The guard app keeps a local copy of the estate's live codes, so a network outage never becomes a gate outage. Entries queue on the phone and sync when the connection returns.
- **Every attempt is logged, including refusals**, with the reason it was refused.
- Residents join with two codes — one for the estate, one for their specific house — and an **estate administrator approves them** before any visitor code can be generated.
- **A code stays inside its estate.** The resident who created it, the guard it is presented to, and that estate's administrators (who can cancel it) can see it. Nobody at another estate can, and the platform's own dashboard never shows a code.
- Residents are **notified when their code is used** at the gate.
- Runs on **ordinary Android and iOS phones**. No turnstiles, scanners or new hardware.
- Estates are **fully isolated from one another**; no estate can see another's residents, codes or gate log.
- **Estate dues** can be billed per resident or per house, paid a month at a time or up to a year ahead. If the estate switches it on, a house in arrears cannot create new visitor codes until it pays; residents keep their own access and codes already sent keep working.
- Pricing is **per home** and quoted after a demo.

## Get the app

The resident app is published on both stores. Visitors install nothing — they
receive a code in a message and read it out at the gate.

- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6811966469) — iPhone and iPad
- [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.myestateaccess.resident) — Android

Downloading it is not enough on its own: signing in requires an estate that
already uses myestateaccess, and an administrator there approves the resident
before any visitor code can be generated.

The guard app is a separate app, on Google Play, and signing into it requires
an active guard membership that an estate administrator grants — downloading
it gives a person nothing on its own.

## Pages

- [Home](https://myestateaccess.com/): what the product does, how a code moves from resident to visitor to guard, and who can see what.
- [About](https://myestateaccess.com/about): the design decisions behind it — why the offline case was built first, why access expires on its own, and why refusals are logged.
- [Contact](https://myestateaccess.com/contact): book a twenty-minute demo at your gate, ask about pricing, rollout and support.
- [Privacy policy](https://myestateaccess.com/privacy): what is collected from residents, guards and administrators, who can see it, how long it is kept, and rights under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.
- [Delete your account](https://myestateaccess.com/delete-account): how to erase an account and what the estate's security log retains.

## Terms used

- **Visitor code** — the short one-time code a resident generates and forwards to a visitor.
- **Estate code** — identifies an estate when a resident signs up.
- **House code** — identifies one home within an estate, so a resident lands in the right household.
- **Gate log** — the record of every verification attempt at the gate, successful or refused.
